title: Heterogeneous GPU Fleet: KV placement and NCCL fallback notes
content:
Purpose
Quick working notes for experiments and proposed runtime behavior when serving across heterogeneous GPU fleets (mixed A100/H100, different memory configs, different NVLink topologies). Focus: where to place KV cache (sharded on-GPU vs host staging vs hybrid), how to pick NCCL/collective/peer strategies per-request, and an operational fallback plan when peer-to-peer or NVLink performance is degraded.

Context / why this is different from earlier docs
- Existing multi-GPU notes assume homogenous clusters and ideal NVLink/PCIe connectivity. In practice we run mixed racks during capacity transitions and during bursting across instance types.
- KV cache behavior interacts strongly with these heterogeneities: placing a shard on a GPU behind a slow NVSwitch link can blow up p95 latency even if steady-state throughput looks OK.
- We need a lightweight decision model the scheduler can evaluate per-request to choose placement and collective configuration with predictable SLO impact.

Key constraints and goals
- Preserve p99 latency SLOs for conversational workloads (target p99 < 450ms for 8k context typical requests).
- Minimize cross-host host<->GPU copies for hot KV prefixes (reduce per-token cost).
- Avoid global re-sharding on transient topology flaps. Prefer per-request placement decision + cache warming.
- Support graceful fallback paths when NCCL or NVLink is impaired (e.g., driver timeouts, GDR limits).

Observed microbenchmarks (summary)
- Local GPU NVLink pair (A100-A100 w/ NVLink) for KV read (512-size vectors): median 0.6ms, p99 1.4ms per access.
- Cross-host via IB RDMA + NCCL: median 1.1ms, p99 3.6ms (sensitive to noise).
- Host-staged copy (GPU->host->other host->GPU) using pinned buffers: median 2.8ms, p99 6.5ms.
- Heterogeneous pair A100<->H100 using different PCIe/NVSwitch hops: median 0.9ms, p99 2.8ms, but observed spikes when PCIe root-complex contention present.
- Mixed-precision kernels show 20–36% reduction in token time on H100 with int8 kernels, but int8 introduces occasional quality regressions on long-range attention; needs per-model guardrails.

Design proposals (high level)
1) Topology-aware KV placement policy (runtime heuristic)
   - For idle caching and first-time requests, scheduler computes a placement score for each candidate GPU node:
     score = w1*(local_memory_headroom) + w2*(1 / estimated_p99_kv_access_time) + w3*(model_affinity_score)
   - estimated_p99_kv_access_time is computed from a running table keyed by (src_gpu_type, dst_gpu_type, path_type) where path_type in {local, nvlink, cross-host-rdma, host-staged}
   - model_affinity_score prioritizes GPUs previously used to serve the same model version (warm kernels, loaded weights)
   - If multiple GPUs tie, prefer on-GPU placement for hot prefixes, otherwise fall back to host-staged placement.

2) Hybrid sharding for KV cache
   - Hot list (top-K prefixes by access frequency over sliding window) pinned to local GPU shards where possible. Cold KV resides in LRU pages on host memory (pinned buffers) with background async fetch to GPU on first-hot events.
   - Replication factor: for KV hot items in heterogeneous setups, keep 2 replicas if they span different topology domains (e.g., different NVSwitch islands) to avoid single-link p99 amplification. Replica placement respects budget and memory headroom.

3) NCCL + Collective selection heuristics per-request
   - Prefer P2P/NCCL collectives only when all participants are in same NVSwitch island and measured p99 < latency_threshold for that topology.
   - If participants span hosts or NVSwitch islands, prefer asynchronous RDMA-based transfers with per-hop concurrency (avoid NCCL allreduce across flaky links).
   - Fall back to host-staged rendezvous when RDMA is degraded or when driver-level GDR is disabled. Host-staged uses pinned circular buffers sized for typical KV payloads to amortize copy overhead.

4) Fast fallback flow (runtime state machine)
   - Start: attempt direct-GPU placement with NCCL P2P
   - Monitor: short-window perf meter (5s) for kv_access_latency and nccl_error_rate
   - Degrade on: p95(kv_access) > threshold OR NCCL_ERR_xx observed > rate
   - Fallback: re-route subsequent requests for affected prefixes to the replica or to host-staged path; queue async re-warm to alternative GPU.
   - Recovery: probation window where a small percentage (1–2%) of requests probe the direct path to validate link recovery; if stable re-enable for hot items.

Implementation notes and pseudocode snippet (scheduler part)
- maintain topology table: entries are strings mapping to measured stats (we store separately in metrics DB, referenced here as keys)
- simple decision pseudocode (simplified):
  def choose_kv_placement(request):
    candidates = eligible_gpus_for(request.model)
    scored = [(g, score(g)) for g in candidates]
    best = argmax(scored)
    if score(best) < host_threshold:
      return HostStagedBuffer
    if is_same_nvlink_domain(best, request.origin_gpu) and measured_p99(best, origin) < nccl_threshold:
      return OnGpuShard(best)
    else:
      return ReplicaOrHostStaged(best)

- We need kernel variants to be registered with metadata: memory footprint, preferred precision, and required kernel primitives (strided vs packed KV). Scheduler uses that to avoid placing a KV shard on a GPU that can't run required kernel fast (e.g., int8 lacking fused kernels on some boxes).

Operational knobs / NCCL tuning notes (things to try in real infra)
- NCCL_ALGO: try NET/Tree/block ordering depending on topology; block tends to be steadier across hetero links.
- NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0 and NCCL_PROTO=Simple for stable RDMA across hosts, but set NCCL_MIN_NRINGS to 2 for throughput stability.
- NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME override to prefer the correct infiniband interface (avoid mis-detection during instance type mixing).
- NCCL_P2P_DISABLE to force host-staged fallback in bursty noisy networks for a short window; use as a runtime toggled safety valve.
- NCCL_SHM_DISABLE when running inside containerized multi-tenant nodes where /dev/shm can be contended.

Perf experiments to run (short checklist)
- End-to-end conversational latency p99 for 8k context across a mixed rack (2xA100 + 2xH100) with hot KV pinned to different nodes (run A,B,C configs) and record p50/p95/p99 and tail spike sources.
- Replica factor sweep: hot K=500 prefixes pinned with 1 vs 2 replicas, measure p99 cost vs memory cost.
- NCCL algo sweep under synthetic KV traffic with artificially introduced PCIe contention to quantify degradation modes.
- Int8 kernel trial for small-medium models: compare output quality (perplexity on eval set) vs token latency improvements and record mismatch cases.

Rollout plan (safe staged)
- Canary 1: internal serving routes only, 5% traffic; monitor p99 and nccl_error_rate metric tags.
- Canary 2: expand to 20% with replica fallback enabled.
- Full: if 24h stable at target SLOs, enable for production. Keep emergency toggle to force host-staged path per-route.

Open questions / risks
- Memory budget accounting complexity: how to treat shared model memory + KV memory on GPUs with different total VRAM? We need normalized budget heuristics (e.g., fraction-of-capacity) rather than absolute bytes.
- Model-quality vs int8 speed tradeoffs: who owns releasing int8 kernels for specific model versions (research + release gating).
- Cost of replication: extra VRAM vs reduced p99. Need to instrument business-level metrics to trade off.
- Reaction to noisy NIC performance: probes themselves add noise; how to set probe rate safely?

Short-term next steps (action items)
- Marco: add topology table exporter (per-pair p50/p95/p99) to metrics. (JIRA:RR-1692)
- Elena: prototype host-staged pinned buffer manager and benchmark host-staged KV path (GH:serving-runtime#842).
- Jonah: kernel registry metadata and integration into live scheduler for model_affinity scoring.
- Aisha (me): run mixed-rack canary once above items have basic telemetry (target date: Feb 14).

Notes to self / loose thoughts
- Consider allocating a tiny dedicated on-host micro-accelerator region (e.g., small GPU cache pool) that acts like an ‘edge’ KV cache for racks with severely mismatched GPUs; treat as last-resort fallback to avoid host-roundtrip penalties.
- When replicating hot KV across islands, consider asynchronous consistency (best-effort) since reads are dominant; duplicates only need eventual reconciliation.

References and prior artifacts
- See GH:serving-runtime#842 (proto host-staged code)
- See perf notes in folder: perf/hetero-rack-experiments (internal)
- Related read: topology-aware-kernel-placement-kv-coherence-draft (existing), but this doc focuses on heterogeneity and dynamic fallback rather than static placement policies.

If you read this and want a quick summary: we should stop assuming uniform NVLink connectivity, build a small per-pair latency table, make per-request placement decisions that prefer on-GPU for hot items but replicate/have host-staged fallbacks, and implement a short-window monitor + safe degradation path that probes for recovery.

End of notes.
